items.reason: Both answers correctly explain that an authenticated tenant claim does not authorize a specific object, and each covers all five core claims, so no judged dimension separates them.

Answer 1 states the legacy destination and also covers the staged timings, the 0.1 completion rate, the 1,080 s mean with censoring at 1,200 s and the maximum divergence, while answer 2 covers only the destination and drain.

Answer 1 covers bidirectional semantic comparison, single-writer authority across intermediate states and approval plus rehearsed recovery in depth, whereas answer 2 concentrates on the controlled-cutover preconditions and leaves several core claims only sketched.

Answer 1 covers the signal dependency, the contraindication, writer-to-cache fan-out costs, TTL bounds and the post-write window, while answer 2 omits the fan-out breadth and the rejection where read-after-write is hard.

Answer 1 covers the interval formula, coverage assumptions, calibration statuses and derived-status inheritance, while answer 2 states the sampling-versus-input distinction but omits correlation and heavy-tail failures, the recording fields and status inheritance.
